content: {"items":[{"statement":"A series of coastal toponyms documented on maps or utilized in the modern vernacular of Phournoi are probably the living remnants of pirate activity in the past: Kourniachto (a place for hiding or lurking), Kleftolimano (harbor of thieves), Fygou (escape), Fylakio (guard-post), Vardia (shift or guard), Tourkolimnionas (harbor of the Turks), Pano and Kato Maneta (upper and lower Maneta).","evidence_id":"e-a651d645c92ef0849332","passage_ids":[9],"kind":"source_statement","source_type":"SECONDARY_SOURCE","actors":[],"places":[],"dates":[],"usage_type":"RAID_LOCATION","uncertainty":["ORIGINAL_NOT_INSPECTED","SOURCE_GENEALOGY_PENDING","INDEPENDENCE_UNRESOLVED","TOPONYM_AND_USAGE_REQUIRE_SEMANTIC_EXTRACTION"]},{"statement":"The two bays designated as Pano and Kato Maneta, situated roughly in the middle of the eastern coast of the main island of Phournoi, likely derived their names from the Zakynthian corsair Eustathios (Stathis) Romanos or Manetas, who operated as a pirate in the Aegean Sea between 1678 and 1684.","evidence_id":"e-a651d645c92ef0849332","passage_ids":[12],"kind":"source_statement","source_type":"SECONDARY_SOURCE","actors":["Eustathios (Stathis) Romanos or Manetas"],"places":["Phournoi"],"dates":["1678-1684"],"usage_type":"BASE","uncertainty":["ORIGINAL_NOT_INSPECTED","SOURCE_GENEALOGY_PENDING","INDEPENDENCE_UNRESOLVED","TOPONYM_AND_USAGE_REQUIRE_SEMANTIC_EXTRACTION"]}]}
